title: Emrys and the Lantern
premise: In 1813 England, Cyrus Thornbury, a battlefield nurse turned estate workshop clerk, has spent seven years recording in her private ledger the names of soldiers and servants erased from official accounts. When a sealed letter arrives naming the Halloran family as conspirators in an officer's embezzlement scheme, Cyrus realizes her ledger holds the only proof of who truly acted and who was framed. As the family's enemies move to burn the workshop and its records, she must choose between the loyalty that kept her safe and the truth that could destroy or redeem everyone she serves. The novel ends with Cyrus testifying before a magistrate, ledger in hand, saving the innocent Halloran heir while accepting exile for herself, carrying her lantern and her book down a road away from everything she protected.
about_author: P. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing regimental records in provincial English libraries, where the gaps between documents proved more telling than the entries. Emrys and the Lantern is their second novel exploring the quiet people history forgets to write down.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the winter of 1813, Cyrus tends wounded men at the Halloran estate's converted workshop, secretly recording in her ledger the names officers omit from dispatches. Establishes her method: invisibility as survival. Emotional beat: weary competence masking old grief over a brother lost unnamed.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A sealed letter arrives for Lord Halloran, addressed in a hand Cyrus recognizes from her nursing days. She delivers it unopened but glimpses one phrase: 'the Thornbury account.' Fear stirs; someone remembers her name. Beat: dread entering a place of routine.

chapters.title: The Workshop at Dusk
chapters.summary: Emrys Halloran's POV. The younger Halloran son, Emrys, works late restoring a lantern recovered from Balaclava's aftermath, avoiding his father's demands he join the regimental office. He notices Cyrus's lamplight burning past midnight. Beat: two insomniacs circling the same unease.

chapters.title: What Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashback to Crimea, seven years prior: how Cyrus began the ledger after watching a captain claim credit for a dead sergeant's maneuver. Introduces Colonel Vane, then ambitious, now a visiting inspector. Beat: the origin of her quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: Vane Comes to Dinner
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Colonel Vane dines at the estate, all charm and probing questions about the family's wartime finances. Lord Halloran grows brittle. Emrys watches Cyrus serve with perfect blankness and wonders what she sees. Beat: the predator entering the sheepfold politely.

chapters.title: The Ledger's First Page
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus rereads her earliest entries and finds Vane's name threaded through three suspicious supply transactions she documented years ago. The sealed letter may not accuse the Hallorans—it may be bait set by Vane. Beat: the hunter realizing she is also hunted.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A fire nearly takes the estate's record room; only scorched ledgers survive. Lord Halloran orders the workshop cleared of 'useless paper.' Emrys rescues a box and hides it in the lantern workshop. Beat: first open violence, still deniable.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Insomniacs
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Emrys catches Cyrus copying documents by lantern light. Instead of reporting her, he asks what she knows. Uneasy trust forms between master's son and invisible nurse. Beat: loneliness recognizing loneliness.

chapters.title: The Sergeant's Widow
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus visits Martha Quill, widow of the sergeant whose name Vane stole, now living in poverty nearby. Martha confirms Vane visited last month asking about 'the Thornbury woman.' Beat: the past reaching out with cold fingers.

chapters.title: Orders to Clear the Grounds
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Lord Halloran, pressured by Vane, announces the workshop will be demolished by spring and its contents burned—officially to settle debts. Emrys realizes the destruction has a purpose: erasing evidence. Beat: the clock begins ticking.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silences
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus confronts her own complicity: names she never recorded to protect people, including Emrys's father, whose debts funded Vane's early schemes. Her ledger indicts those she loves too. Beat: loyalty and truth begin their war inside her.

chapters.title: The Lantern Lit
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys finishes restoring the lantern—a Crimean field piece engraved with the sergeant Quill's name—and hangs it in the workshop window, a small act of defiance. Beat: memory made visible, hope kindled against orders.

chapters.title: A Summons to London
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Lord Halloran orders Cyrus to accompany him to London to answer Vane's inquiries. She smuggles the ledger's most dangerous pages sewn into her petticoats. Beat: walking into the lion's mouth with the truth hidden against her skin.

chapters.title: The Club Where Names Are Traded
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In London, Cyrus observes Vane at his club, trading favors and forged signatures with a treasury clerk. She copies a name: Aldous Finch, the man who wrote the sealed letter. Beat: the conspiracy acquires faces.

chapters.title: Finch's Confession, Half-Spoken
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV (interleaved with Cyrus's letter home). Emrys tracks down Finch, who admits the letter accusing the Hallorans was dictated to him—but refuses to say by whom, terrified. Beat: a witness found, and already breaking.

chapters.title: The Price of Protection
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Lord Halloran offers Cyrus money and passage abroad if she surrenders any papers concerning the family. She lies smoothly for the first time to a man she respects. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Martha's Testimony
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Martha Quill agrees to swear what she saw in Crimea—if Cyrus can guarantee her safety. Cyrus cannot, honestly. She promises anyway. Beat: the cost of recruiting allies into danger.

chapters.title: Fire in the Outbuildings
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A second fire destroys the stable records. This time a hired man is seen fleeing toward Vane's lodgings. Lord Halloran, broken, finally tells Emrys the truth of his debts to Vane. Beat: the family's shame laid bare, father and son estranged and bound at once.

chapters.title: The Page That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus discovers pages torn from her own ledger—someone has been in her room. Only three people had access. Paranoia blooms; she moves the ledger into the lantern workshop wall. Beat: betrayal at close range.

chapters.title: Emrys Chooses
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys finds the missing pages hidden in his father's study—Lord Halloran took them, hoping to bargain with Vane. Emrys returns them to Cyrus without his father's knowledge. Beat: the son choosing truth over blood.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Vane corners Cyrus privately: surrender the ledger, and the Hallorans keep their name; refuse, and he'll prove she falsified army records—a hanging offense for forgery. Beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Night Watch
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Cyrus and Emrys keep watch over the workshop through a storm, copying the full ledger by lantern light into duplicate pages hidden separately. Exhausted intimacy; almost-confessions neither completes. Beat: tenderness under siege.

chapters.title: Finch Is Silenced
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. News arrives: Finch fell from a London bridge—an apparent suicide. His confession dies with him unless his written draft survived. Beat: despair; the enemy kills at distance.

chapters.title: The Draft in the Hymnal
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following Finch's earlier hint, Cyrus finds his confession draft hidden in a hymnal he once gave Martha Quill. It names Vane and two treasury clerks. Beat: grief transmuted into ammunition.

chapters.title: Demolition Day Announced
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The magistrate sets the workshop demolition in ten days, and Vane schedules his inspection for the same week—the evidence must be gone before anyone official can see it. Beat: converging deadlines, no room left to hide.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Owes
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus visits her brother's unmarked grave and finally writes his full name in the ledger's front page—her own name beside it. She stops hiding. Beat: the theme crystallized; she claims visibility.

chapters.title: The Father's Bargain
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Lord Halloran meets Vane secretly, offering the stolen ledger pages plus silence in exchange for debt forgiveness. Vane accepts—then has Halloran followed home, planning to implicate him fully regardless. Beat: loyalty repaid with a knife.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Gate
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Constables arrest Lord Halloran for embezzlement on Vane's sworn information. The household scatters. Cyrus watches the family she served destroyed by the very omissions she once recorded. Beat: the floor gives way.

chapters.title: Emrys Stands Alone
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys, now head of a disgraced house, begs Cyrus to flee with the ledger and save herself. She refuses: testimony without the book is hearsay; the book without testimony is theft. Both are needed. Beat: the partnership becomes a pact.

chapters.title: Gathering Witnesses
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus spends three days collecting the living: Martha Quill, a discharged corporal named in her ledger, a former quartermaster's clerk. Each risks something to stand in a courtroom. Beat: the invisible assembling into a chorus.

chapters.title: The Wall Comes Down Early
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Vane accelerates the demolition—workmen arrive at dawn. Emrys physically blocks the crew while Cyrus retrieves the ledger from the wall cavity. He is struck and bloodied; the lantern shatters. Beat: sacrifice; the symbol breaks so the truth survives.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Fen
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus and Emrys escape across frozen fenland with the ledger and Finch's draft, pursued by Vane's hired men. A near-drowning at a drainage cut; Emrys saves the book, nearly losing himself. Beat: terror and devotion fused.

chapters.title: Sanctuary and Strategy
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Sheltered by Martha Quill, they prepare for the assizes: ledger entries cross-referenced, witnesses rehearsed, Finch's draft authenticated by his own handwriting in the hymnal margins. Beat: the calm before judgment.

chapters.title: Vane's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Vane files charges against Cyrus for forgery of army records, producing doctored samples. Her arrest warrant is issued. She can testify and be taken, or run and let the Hallorans hang alone. Beat: the trap closes on its author.

chapters.title: The Assizes Open
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The trial of Lord Halloran begins. Vane performs magnificently. Emrys, barred as kin, waits outside the courtroom listening to doors. Beat: helplessness sharpening into fury.

chapters.title: Cyrus Takes the Stand
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus surrenders herself and testifies, reading names aloud from the ledger—dead sergeants, unpaid widows, forged signatures—each entry dated in her own hand. The courtroom goes silent around the small voices of the forgotten. Beat: climax; memory wielded as power.

chapters.title: The Unraveling
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Martha and the corporal corroborate; the hymnal draft matches Finch's hand; a treasury clerk, facing ruin, turns crown's evidence against Vane. Vane's composure cracks publicly. Beat: the corruption devouring itself.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Lord Halloran is convicted of debt fraud but spared conspiracy; Vane is arrested for forgery and the death of Finch. Cyrus's forgery charge is dismissed—her ledger ruled a true record. Beat: justice partial, real, and costly.

chapters.title: The Lantern Rehung
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Spring: the workshop stands, spared by the new magistrate. Emrys rehangs a rebuilt lantern in the window, Quill's name reground into the glass. Lord Halloran, diminished, begins restitution. Beat: quiet restoration; memory given a home.

chapters.title: Down the Long Road
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Though cleared, Cyrus chooses exile—her testimony made her too visible to stay invisible, and some silences keep others safe. Emrys gives her a new lantern and a blank second ledger. She walks the north road, writing names as she goes. Beat: bittersweet resolution; the work continues, carried forward.
